kurz: Cornmeal [[quellen|swells]] slowly in plenty of liquid into a creamy porridge: stirring prevents lumps, time makes it soft.
bild_im_kopf: Like dry earth after a long steady rain: it turns soft and creamy.

schluesselmomente.schritt: Rain the cornmeal into boiling salted water or stock while stirring, about 1 : 4 for soft polenta (as a guide)
schluesselmomente.warum: Each grain should enter the water separately. A lump gelatinises on the outside and stays dry inside.

schluesselmomente.schritt: Cook on low heat for 30–45 minutes, stirring now and then
schluesselmomente.warum: Coarse maize needs time for the starch inside to swell.

schluesselmomente.schritt: Stir in butter and cheese at the end
schluesselmomente.warum: Fat and cheese make the polenta smooth and round off the flavour.

schluesselmomente.schritt: Spread leftovers on a tray, let them set and fry them
schluesselmomente.warum: As it cools, the starch rearranges and sets.
